newsitem.title: MOZAMBIQUE: French firm to develop run-down Mozambican hotel.
newsitem.headline: French firm to develop run-down Mozambican hotel.

text.p: Work is to begin in January to turn one of Mozambique's most famous eyesores into the country's first Holiday Inn hotel, government sources said on Monday.
The plan for a French company to complete construction of the "Four Seasons" hotel was announced at a conference in Maputo last May but there were few details at the time.
A French construction company, Sipie Batignolles T.P., signed a contract on Friday to start work before the middle of January, the sources told Reuters.
The multi-story Maputo beachfront hotel was built before Mozambique's independence in 1975. But it had no balconies overlooking the picturesque Maputo bay.

It was decided soon after independence that balconies were essential so all the seaview window surroundings were broken to enable the work to be done. But the money ran out and only the destruction, not the construction, was carried out.
The shell remained as an ugly blot on the landscape.
The French company's deal is with ECOTUR, the Mozambican-South African venture that now holds the concession on the hotel.
The cost of the building work is estimated at $40 million.
The hotel should be complete in the second half of 1998. It will be a 340-bed luxury hotel with swimming pool, conference hall and casino. It will be managed by the Holiday Inn chain.
